title: Fitting a fascia board and soffit
subtitle: Replace or renew the fascia board and soffit at the eaves of a roof to seal the rafter feet and provide a fixing point for the guttering
excerpt: How to replace a fascia board and soffit at the eaves of a pitched roof. Covers removing the old boards safely, preparing the rafter feet, fitting the ventilated soffit, cutting and fixing the fascia, and sealing the joints.
sourceNotes: Collins Complete DIY Manual (referenced, not reproduced). UK trade practice for roofline replacement and NHBC Standards Chapter 7 (referenced, not reproduced).

glossaryTerms.definition: The vertical board fixed to the ends of the roof rafters at the eaves. It closes off the rafter ends, gives a fixing point for the gutter, and forms the visible front face of the roofline. In older construction it is painted softwood; in modern replacement work it is typically 16 to 25 mm uPVC.

The horizontal board or panel running under the fascia between the fascia face and the external wall. It closes off the open rafter bay, preventing birds and vermin from entering the roof space. Ventilated soffit panels or continuous soffit vents are used where the roof requires through-ventilation.

is the horizontal board beneath the fascia that closes the gap between the fascia and the external wall. INTERMEDIATE: the work is done on a ladder; all cuts need to land on rafter feet or fixing points.
Remove the old boards and guttering

Unhook and remove the gutter sections. Pull away the old fascia board by unscrewing or levering carefully. The soffit will either clip out or be nailed to the back of the fascia. Remove both together where they are one piece. Take care not to damage the roof tiles at the eaves: the lowest course of tiles may overhang the old fascia.

Inspect each rafter foot for rot. Test with a bradawl: any rafter that takes the bradawl point easily is soft and must be repaired before the new boards go on. Sound rafter feet need only a coat of preservative primer on the end grain. If the rafter ends are uneven in height, mark a level line across them and plane or chisel the high rafter feet down to the line.

For a uPVC soffit system, fit the J-section receiving channel to the wall first, checking it is level. Measure the soffit width between the channel and the fascia fixing position at each rafter. Cut the soffit panel to width, allowing for the thermal expansion gap specified by the manufacturer. Slide the inner edge into the J-channel and bring the outer edge to the rafter feet line.

Offer the fascia board up to the rafter ends, with the bottom edge trapping the outer edge of the soffit panel in its groove. The top of the fascia should sit level with or just below the top of the last rafter so the underside of the roof tile batten bears correctly. Fix through the fascia into each rafter end with two 65 mm stainless screws at each point. Cut the joints between fascia board lengths on a rafter foot so both cut ends are supported.

attrs.symptom: Fascia board bows in the run between rafter fixing points
attrs.cause: The rafter centres are wider than 600 mm, or the board is too thin for the span.
attrs.fix: Fix an additional noggin between rafters behind the board at the mid-span point, and add a screw into the noggin to pull the bow out.

attrs.symptom: Gap visible between the soffit and the wall at the J-channel
attrs.cause: The wall is not straight in the horizontal plane and the J-channel follows the wall rather than being set level.
attrs.fix: Pack the J-channel away from the wall at low points to bring it to a level line, then fill the gap behind with expanding foam or flexible filler.
